directions.label: Understand molecules
directions.subtitle: Representations & molecular state
directions.question: How can an AI maintain an explicit molecular state?
directions.description: I study how structures, fragments, and language can share a grounded representation—so a model can describe a molecule and make precise changes to it.
directions.principle: Start with an explicit molecular state.

works.name: MolReFlect
works.description: Fine-grained alignment of molecules and text.

directions.label: Reason with evidence
directions.subtitle: Chemical reasoning & verification
directions.question: Which steps in chemical reasoning can we actually check?
directions.description: I connect chemical reasoning with explicit intermediate states and verification, while investigating when a convincing chain of thought becomes an unreliable explanation.

works.name: Chemical CoT
works.description: Testing the faithfulness of the scratchpad.

directions.label: Work through tools
directions.subtitle: Scientific agents & workflows
directions.question: How does a scientific intention become executable work?
directions.description: I study agents that turn molecular design goals into tool calls, code, and research workflows, and evaluate whether the resulting artifacts do the intended scientific job.
directions.principle: Connect an intention to a reproducible artifact.

works.name: Molecular LLM Agents
works.description: Architectures and levels of scientific autonomy.

directions.label: Test the limits
directions.subtitle: Generalization & trustworthy autonomy
directions.question: When should a scientist trust the system—and when should they step in?
directions.description: I examine structural perturbations, reasoning failures, and domain-specific evaluation to map the limits of model competence across molecular science, physics, and medicine.

works.name: Molecular Generalization
works.description: Probing local trust regions with graph edits.

works.name: Medical Reasoning
works.description: Aligning clinical needs and AI capabilities.

papers.name: MolLean
papers.takeaway: Chemical reasoning, checked step by step.
papers.sketch_alt: Molecular state, a chemical step, and a kernel check connected by arrows.
papers.title: MolLean: A Process-Verifiable Language for Chemical Reasoning
papers.summary: A state-grounded chemical reasoning language whose Lean-based kernel checks molecular transitions and assertions, with whole-trace and interactive feedback.

papers.name: STAMP
papers.takeaway: A molecular language built from reusable fragments.
papers.sketch_alt: A tree of colored molecular fragments connected through attachment sites.
papers.title: STAMP as a topology-aware molecular language for fragment-level learning and editing
papers.authors: Yuxuan Ren, Jiatong Li, Ziqiao Meng, Yatao Bian
papers.summary: A fragment-tree molecular language that makes motifs, attachment sites, and topology explicit for representation learning and executable editing.

papers.name: Molecular LLM Agents
papers.takeaway: From tool-using assistants to scientific autonomy.
papers.sketch_alt: A scientific agent connects a plan to tools and evidence through a feedback loop.
papers.title: Molecular LLM Agents: From Architectural Design to Scientific Autonomy
papers.authors: Jiatong Li, Wengyu Zhang, Weida Wang, Yuxuan Ren, Wei Liu, Chenyang Mao, et al.
papers.summary: A unified architecture for molecular LLM agents and a four-level autonomy ladder spanning assistive workflows to scientific-agenda agents.

papers.name: Chemical CoT
papers.takeaway: A useful scratchpad. An unreliable explanation.
papers.sketch_alt: A structural scratchpad and an explanation are separated by a question of faithfulness.
papers.title: Chemical Chain-of-Thought Functions as a Hallucination-Prone Molecular Scratchpad
papers.authors: Jiatong Li, Yuxuan Ren, Weida Wang, Xiaoyong Wei, Yatao Bian
papers.summary: Chemical CoT can be causally useful as a structural scratchpad while remaining an unreliable explanation of how an answer was reached.

papers.name: Molecular Generalization
papers.takeaway: How far does molecular understanding generalize?
papers.sketch_alt: Two related graphs differ by a highlighted edit within a local neighborhood.
papers.title: Do LLMs Truly Generalize in the Molecular Domain? A Perturbation-Based Analysis
papers.authors: Jiatong Li, Weida Wang, Changmeng Zheng, Shufei Zhang, Yatao Bian, Xiao-yong Wei, Qing Li
papers.summary: Controlled graph edits reveal a narrow local trust region in molecular LLMs and show how in-context tuning can partially stabilize it.

papers.name: Medical Reasoning
papers.takeaway: Connecting clinical needs with model capabilities.
papers.sketch_alt: Two overlapping lenses connect clinical needs with model capabilities.
papers.title: Aligning Clinical Needs and AI Capabilities: A Survey on LLMs for Medical Reasoning
papers.authors: Qi Peng*, Jiatong Li*, Sirui Huang, Yiyang Jiang, Kaisong Gong, et al.
papers.summary: A dual clinical–computational view of medical reasoning, paired with a five-level benchmark across 18 state-of-the-art models.

papers.name: MolViBench
papers.takeaway: Can generated code do useful molecular science?
papers.sketch_alt: A coding window connects scientific intent to an executable molecular workflow.
papers.title: MolViBench: Evaluating LLMs on Molecular Vibe Coding
papers.authors: Jiatong Li, Yuxuan Ren, Weida Wang, Changmeng Zheng, Xiao-yong Wei, Qing Li, Yatao Bian
papers.summary: A benchmark for executable molecular coding across 12 real-world drug-discovery workflows.

papers.name: Speak-to-Structure
papers.takeaway: One design brief. Many possible molecules.
papers.sketch_alt: A natural-language design brief branches into three molecular graph candidates.
papers.title: Speak-to-Structure: Open-Domain Natural Language-Driven Molecule Generation
papers.authors: Jiatong Li*, Junxian Li*, Yunqing Liu, Dongzhan Zhou, Qing Li
papers.summary: S²-Bench evaluates one-to-many molecular design from natural-language requirements.

papers.name: Chem-R
papers.takeaway: Learning to reason like a chemist.
papers.sketch_alt: Three stacked training stages lead from chemical foundations to reasoning and optimization.
papers.title: Chem-R: Learning to Reason as a Chemist
papers.authors: Weida Wang, Benteng Chen, Di Zhang, et al., Jiatong Li, et al.
papers.summary: A three-phase chemical reasoning model spanning molecular- and reaction-level tasks.

papers.name: MolReFlect
papers.takeaway: Aligning molecular details with their descriptions.
papers.sketch_alt: Colored parts of a molecular graph align with matching phrases in a text.
papers.title: MolReFlect: Fine-Grained Alignments Between Molecules and Texts
papers.authors: Jiatong Li, Yunqing Liu, Wei Liu, Jingdi Lei, Di Zhang, Wenqi Fan, et al.
papers.summary: An in-context reflection framework for precise molecule–text alignment.

papers.name: CMPhysBench
papers.takeaway: Putting calculation-intensive reasoning to the test.
papers.sketch_alt: A condensed-matter lattice sits beside a notebook of mathematical calculations.
papers.title: CMPhysBench: Evaluating LLMs in Condensed Matter Physics
papers.authors: Weida Wang*, Dongchen Huang*, Jiatong Li*, Tengchao Yang, et al.
papers.summary: A fine-grained benchmark for calculation-intensive reasoning in condensed matter physics.
